A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REGLUE work and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting and movement between the main text and supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, compressor and guidance ablations, and Cityscapes semantic-preservation results in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Food-101 and ImageNet-512 evaluations, frequency analysis, compute measurements, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed compressor, global/local/VAE fusion, velocity and alignment objectives, and sampling procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. Newly evaluated fusion, compression, and regularization variants are diagnostic ablations; they do not replace the proposed architecture or training objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds focused food-image generation on Food-101 and higher-resolution ImageNet generation at 512×512 (Appendix A.7, Table 14). v1's generation experiments cover ImageNet at 256×256. Existing Cityscapes probing and reduced-data ImageNet experiments are retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds RAE and REPA-E to the retained comparison methods, flagging their different latent spaces and the class-balanced evaluation of the 800-epoch REPA-E result. Table 1 also adds PCA-based combinations with global tokens, alignment, and multi-layer features as explicit comparison controls.

E3.justification: The stated default CFG scale changes from 2.8 to 2.3, retaining the guidance interval and sampling steps. v2 substantially expands evaluation through CMMD, DINOv2-based FD/FD-infinity, inference throughput, total training compute, and additional compression/fusion/resampling controls. Existing main training budgets and the 50,000-sample evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds matched PCA combination controls, a frequency-profile diagnostic, alternative-metric checks, compute-efficiency analysis, and fusion/resampling ablations (Table 1, Figure 3, Tables 11 and 13–16). The KL study expands to multiple weights and probing accuracy, while the GAN-loss experiment is removed. The CFG sweep expands; earlier channel, layer, VFM, and limited-data analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional metrics in v2 are presented as point estimates, without a newly described uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Food-101 FID 4.6 versus REG's 7.6 and ImageNet-512 FID 14.4 versus 18.1, plus new metric, compute, and ablation entries. Table 4's 80/160-epoch REGLUE FIDs change from 1.61/1.53 to 1.59/1.46 alongside the changed CFG setting, so these are not identical-setting gains. At the retained CFG scale 2.7, FID changes from 1.53 to 1.52. Main unguided benchmark FIDs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, interpolation assumptions, token definitions, and training objectives retain the same mathematical content. The new frequency analysis is empirical; no theorem, proof, or formal derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about global–local entanglement, nonlinear semantic compression, complementary alignment, and faster convergence. New experiments provide additional support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive mechanism explanation linking high-frequency suppression to diffusability and interprets stronger KL regularization as damaging semantic content. It also discusses metric dependence, compute efficiency, and fusion tradeoffs. Appendix C narrows the outstanding high-resolution limitation to larger models and adds mixed preliminary results from jointly decoding semantic and VAE latents.

D1.justification: v2 specifies throughput measurement on one A100 with batch size 64 and clarifies inclusion of DINOv2 and the compressor in compute accounting. Compressor-size reporting is explicitly reframed around encoder counts in Table 6. Most architecture, optimization, hardware/training-time disclosures, and the code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning Food-101, alternative evaluation metrics, diffusability, encoder/tokenizer alignment, and representation autoencoders, while removing the EQ-VAE citation. The related-work narrative and central positioning relative to REPA, ReDi, and REG remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most abstract, introduction, method, and conclusion wording and section order are retained. Changes concentrate on local experimental explanations, revised captions and cross-references, renamed or added appendix subsections, and a supplementary title page and contents list.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. The overview moves later, and the compressor diagram and convergence samples move into the supplement. v2 adds the frequency plot and several tables and expands existing table columns and rows. The final sample grids retain the same images.

improvement.justification: Matched PCA controls and the frequency diagnostic substantially strengthen evidence isolating the compressor's contribution. Total-compute accounting addresses the limits of v1's iteration-based efficiency evidence, while Food-101, ImageNet-512, and alternative metrics broaden validation. These additions strengthen central design and efficiency claims. Removing the GAN ablation narrows one analysis, and uncertainty reporting remains absent; the retuned CFG scores also require qualification. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
